name: Caffeine (topical)
lead: Topical caffeine is included in many under-eye creams and serums intended to reduce puffiness and dark circles. It is the same xanthine alkaloid found in coffee and tea, used here at low concentrations in a cosmetic base.
The effect is cosmetic and temporary. Some small studies show reduced swelling and improved appearance, but the evidence is limited and often uses short follow-up and company-run designs.

paras: Caffeine is a vasoconstrictor that narrows small vessels, which may reduce visible blood pooling and fluid in the thin periorbital skin. It may also act as an antioxidant and may promote lipolysis and drainage in tissue, although penetration through skin is modest and effects are short-lived.

Topical use is usually well tolerated, with occasional irritation or allergy. Contact with the eyes should be avoided. Absorbed amounts are small, but product claims are often stronger than the evidence, and the effect does not address structural causes of eye bags such as fat prolapse.
